plan.name: Kimi Code
plan.says: Kimi: "Kimi Code subscriptions are for interactive use only" (scripted batch runs are named as beyond normal use), and "Don't spoof or alter client identity information".

presets.note: Moonshot's Kimi Code membership (Plus and above), with a key from the Kimi Code console (the pay-as-you-go platform is the moonshot preset; their keys don't work on each other). K3.1 Pro answers only with its thinking on. In mainland China: --base-url https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1.

plan.name: Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan (legacy)
plan.says: Alibaba: "This plan is for interactive use in programming tools such as Claude Code, Qoder and OpenClaw. Do not use the plan's API key for automated scripts, application backends, or other non-interactive scenarios."

presets.note: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio's (Bailian's) Coding Plan, now sold as legacy (Pro only); its successor is the alibaba-token preset. Outside mainland China: --base-url https://coding-intl.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1.

plan.name: Alibaba Cloud Token Plan (Personal)
plan.says: Alibaba: "Token Plan is for interactive use only in coding tools and agent tools… and must not be used for automation scripts, custom application backends, or any non-interactive batch call scenarios."

presets.note: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio's Token Plan (Lite $6 to Pro $43 a month, sold from Singapore), with an sk-sp- key of its own. In mainland China: --base-url https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1.

plan.name: OpenCode Go
plan.says: OpenCode: "OpenCode Go is designed for OpenCode and other coding agents that produce similar types of requests", each identifying itself "with its own user agent".

presets.note: OpenCode Go ($10 a month; Go Plus $40), on your OpenCode Console key at its own address (pay-as-you-go has another). Each model has a monthly allowance, a fifth of it in any five hours and half in a week. DeepSeek's models want Global chosen under Regions in the Console.

plan.name: Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan
plan.says: Xiaomi: the quota "is only available for use in programming tools (such as OpenClaw, OpenCode, etc.), and it is prohibited to use it in the form of API calls for request behaviors in obvious non-coding scenarios such as automated scripts and custom application backends."

presets.note: Xiaomi MiMo's Token Plan (Lite $6 to Max $100 a month), with a tp- key of its own (ttp- for a team): the pay-as-you-go sk- key doesn't work here. Its address is the one your Token Plan page shows: Europe --base-url https://token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com/v1, mainland China https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1.

plan.name: MiniMax M Plan
plan.says: MiniMax: "M Plan is designed for individual, interactive developer use", in AI tools "such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, and OpenClaw"; "Pay-as-you-go is recommended for production use."

presets.note: MiniMax's M Plan (once its Coding Plan), with an sk-cp- key of its own, apart from the pay-as-you-go one. In mainland China: --base-url https://api.minimax.cn/v1.

plan.name: Volcengine Ark Coding Plan
plan.says: Volcengine: the quota "仅在 AI 编程工具中生效，不可用于 API 调用" (works only inside AI coding tools, never for API calls), and use outside them may be treated as abuse, suspending the subscription.

presets.note: ByteDance's Volcengine Ark Coding Plan (mainland China), on your ordinary Ark key: it is the plan only at this address (…/api/v3 bills the same key as ordinary use).

plan.name: BytePlus ModelArk Coding Plan
plan.says: BytePlus: "Not available for API calls." "Using the Coding Plan–provided Base URL and API key outside AI coding tools may be identified as abuse or a policy violation".

presets.note: BytePlus ModelArk's Coding Plan (ByteDance's, outside China), on your ordinary ModelArk key: it is the plan only at this address.

plan.name: StepFun Step Plan
plan.says: StepFun: "you may not access, invoke, or use the subscribed paid services through unofficial, unauthorized, or unspecified tools"; the tools it names include Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw.

presets.note: StepFun's Step Plan (Flash Mini $6.99 to Flash Max $99 a month, no time windows), on your ordinary Step key: it is the plan only at this address.

plan.name: Tencent Cloud Coding Plan
plan.says: Tencent: "严禁 API 调用" (API calls strictly forbidden): only inside coding tools, never for automated scripts, custom application backends or any non-interactive batch calls.

presets.note: Tencent Cloud's Coding Plan (mainland China). Its key's sk-sp- form is the same as Alibaba's plans', so it is never guessed from a key: add it as this preset.

plan.name: Baidu Qianfan Token Plan (Personal)
plan.says: Baidu: "仅限在兼容的AI编程和智能体工具中交互式使用，不可用于自动化脚本或应用后端" (interactive use only, in compatible AI coding and agent tools; never automated scripts or application backends).

presets.note: Baidu Qianfan's Token Plan (mainland China), with a key of its own.

NanoGPT. Its Pro subscription ($12 a month: 60M input tokens a week on the open models it includes, their output free) is for personal, non-commercial use only, by its terms. Set the key to bill the subscription only, or what it doesn't include is paid as you go.
Synthetic's subscriptions (Go $9, Standard $30, Big $90 a month; weekly limits that refill as you go) put no rule on what calls them. Models are named hf:<org>/<model>, e.g. hf:zai-org/GLM-5.3.
Ollama's cloud models, with your account's API key. Pro ($20 a month) and Max ($100) are prepaid usage at each model's own rates, not a flat allowance.

Cloudflare AI Gateway's OpenAI-compatible endpoint: --base-url https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/<account id>/<gateway id>/compat. The key is the gateway's token; the providers' own keys stay stored in Cloudflare. Models are named <provider>/<model>, e.g. deepseek/deepseek-chat.
Verda's inference API, with an inference API key from its console. A serverless container of your own on Verda has an address of its own: --base-url <its address>/v1.
llama.cpp's llama-server on its default address (127.0.0.1:9931). One started with --port, an older build (8080) or its Docker image takes --base-url.
